What a listing does not tell you

  • How long is the trip to work or school?
  • Is the air clean? Is it quiet at night?
  • Are there nurseries, doctors, parks?
  • What do flats really sell for here?

What exists today

  • Listing portalsFlats, not neighbourhoods
  • Address toolsOne address at a time
  • Price sitesNumbers without the rest of life

Market scan, 3 October 2026: Otodom Analytics, MiejscoMetr, Locumo, Dobra Lokacja, PolandRent.

(Click) Open any property site and you get offers. Hundreds of flats, and nothing on what living there is like. (Click) The questions people actually have go unanswered: the trip to work, the air and the noise, nurseries and doctors, what flats really sell for. The answers exist, but they sit in separate public sources, in different formats and dates. (Click) Today's tools each cover a piece: listing portals show flats, address tools score one address, price sites show prices. Nobody answers the first question: which part of the city fits my life.

So we turn the order around. (Click) Start with your needs: pick a profile or say what matters. See the districts that fit, ranked and explained. Only then look at flats, on any site you like. (Click) GdzieZamieszkać is not a listings site: no offers, no brokers, no ads, and no login. It is free, in Polish by default with English on a toggle. This is the real home page: the city in 18 districts, on one map.

The score is computed in code and tested. AI never computes it.

This is Find a district. (Click) 18 districts, 51 measures in seven categories, nine ready profiles: student, family, senior, remote worker, tight budget and more. (Click) Pick a profile, or say how much each category matters, from 0 to 5. The ranking is percentile ranks within Kraków, weighted your way, and every place says which measures moved it. 47 of the 51 measures have data for Kraków; the other four say why. (Click) The score is computed in code and covered by tests. A language model never computes it.

Back to our family. This is the real output of the Family profile. Podgórze, where the job is, comes 18th for a family. (Click) The top three are Bieńczyce, Mistrzejowice and Łagiewniki-Borek Fałęcki, and each district page gives the public transport time to Podgórze: about 40 minutes. (Click) Every district page has sale prices from actual deeds in the national price register, quarter by quarter, not asking prices. It also has commute times to every district, a rent versus buy estimate, and similar districts.
GdzieZamieszkać

Every number shows its trail. Missing data says why.

  • Every value is measured, estimated or approximate, with its caveat.
  • District level, not address. The data is not that precise, so we don't pretend.
  • No price forecast. Two methods lost to a naive baseline, so we show the history.
  • “Recorded crimes per 10 000 residents”. Never “safe” or “dangerous”.
This is what makes it trustworthy. Open any value and you see what kind it is, its date, source, method, licence and credit line. (Click) Where there is no data, the app says so and why. Kraków does not publish crime figures by district, so we show none, and we never show a zero in place of a gap. (Click) Every value carries its kind: measured, estimated or approximate. We score districts, not addresses, because address-level precision would be false. We show no price forecast: we tested two methods and neither beat a naive baseline. And we say recorded crimes per 10 000 residents, never safe or dangerous.

AI writes the words. Code owns the numbers.

  1. Facts computed in code, stored
  2. A language model writes the report
  3. A guard rejects any number not in the facts
  4. Every AI text carries a label
  • No login. The data service stores nothing about its users.
  • Your typed needs for a personal summary are neither stored nor logged.
  • Profiles only set weights. They never sort people by who lives where.
Here is the role of AI, and it is checkable. (Click) Facts are computed in code. A language model turns them into a readable report. A guard rejects any text with a number that is not in the facts, and every AI text carries a label, as you see on the real district page. The same guard runs on the personal summary, where you type what you need. (Click) Privacy: there is no login, the data service stores nothing about its users, and the text you type is neither stored nor logged. Profiles only set weights. They never filter by who lives in a district.

A public service the city can host.

Built on public data the city and the state already publish

BIP KrakówKraków open dataZTP and MPK timetablesKraków noise map Real estate price register (GUGiK)Air quality (GIOŚ)Nursery registerPolice accident registerCopernicus (EU)OpenStreetMap

What a city host adds

Free for every resident, no loginA public service, not a product
Resident feedback builtKept unverified and unpublished until identity checks through the national login
Official notices and demand by district conceptPlanned projects, and anonymous counts of where people want to live
This is the Smart City part. (Click) Everything runs on public data that Kraków and the state already publish: the city's open data and BIP, the timetables of ZTP and MPK, the city noise map, the national price register, air quality from GIOŚ, the nursery register, the police accident register, and EU Copernicus. (Click) A city is the natural host. It is free and needs no login. Residents can already send feedback, such as the rent they pay; it stays unverified and unpublished until identity checks through the national login exist, and it never changes a score. Official notices and anonymous demand counts by district are concepts, and we show no fake data for them.

What we brought, what we built here, what comes next.

Before HackYeah · 29 Sep to 2 Oct

  • Data collection and the database for 18 districts
  • Read-only data API, 16 operations, with tests

At HackYeah · 3 and 4 Oct

  • The app: map, find, district, compare, feedback
  • City service: personal AI summary, resident feedback
  • Accessibility checks, documents, changelog

Next

  • Run it on a city server
  • Legal opinion: fees, AI transparency (EU AI Act, Art. 50)
  • National login for verified feedback
  • Data-sharing agreements for rents
  • A second city
Our ask: let Kraków host GdzieZamieszkać as a free public service.
